scope: Complete fir2dim_main source-level array-access accounting with externally supplied compute/private-service interval bounds, in a fork/join refresh co-runner model. Not native kernel timing, machine-instruction WCET, or a cache hierarchy model.
kernel_entry: fir2dim_main; fir2dim_init and return wrapper outside selected kernel
source: TACLeBench commit ffdc3f58c9d8f6c1d7e700f2190992c71a3276fe, fir2dim.c; original hash c0f06e2396560c61417d70950360604207f37a144b900b3bb3d186f6a51d7cec
event_accounting: Instrument every explicit source-level global array read/write in both pin_down calls, convolution and checksum. Compiler registers, stack and instruction fetch are represented by supplied compute/private-service bounds, not asserted measured. All arrays outside the shared input read partition use bounded local/private service.
prepare_cleanup: First pin_down is serial preparation before co-runner launch; second pin_down is serial cleanup after both tasks join. Thus no private receiver writes to concurrently shared input partition. Both costs are added to all baselines.
functional_check: Compile original and fully instrumented source separately, both must return zero and instrumented checksum must equal 14. Model refresher version values are abstract, so model does not assert concurrent floating-point output equivalence.
marker_helper_order: Before each noninitial phase marker, including if K unchanged. Fixed policy incurs no dynamic helper cost; every actual load change costs the model registered write cycle.
fixed_domain: All 255 legal K loads, four possible free boundary-flush subsets, and free end release. Enumerate and admit each against same external budget.
phase_control: All 7^3 phase load vectors, same end release. Selection at phi=0 only, freeze chosen policy and evaluate all phi=0..9.
metrics: Full kernel completion = serial preparation + max(receiver body, refresher body) + serial cleanup. Also receiver bound/cycles, shared-memory bound, unknown/hits/evictions, marker costs and admissible policy counts. Retain all empty feasible sets, wins, ties and losses.
limitations: Source-event model has supplied timing bounds and partition placement; coefficient/output/instruction/stack competition is represented by private bounds, not unified L1 cache allocation. No full-system/native throughput claim. Only clean receiver replacement, retained writer ownership and nonallocating WUs are modeled.
